chunks: And he (peace be upon him) said:
When you are turning away (from the world) and death is approaching, how swift is the meeting.

key_terms.إِدْبَار: Turning away or departing (from the world)

ai.seo_question: What does it mean to be in 'idbar' (turning away) when death is approaching?
ai.summary: In this concise maxim from Nahj al-Balagha, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) employs the spatial metaphor of 'turning away' (for worldly pursuits) and 'approaching' (for death) to illustrate the accelerating convergence of the soul with its end. This imagery underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on *zuhd* (asceticism) not as mere withdrawal, but as a conscious realignment of priorities in the face of mortality's inevitability. The brevity of the statement reflects the rhetorical style of the sermons, urging immediate spiritual readiness rather than procrastination.

en.sayed-ali-raza: 29. Amīr al-mu’minīn, peace be upon him, said:
When you are running away from the world and death is approaching, there is no question of delay in the encounter.
